description: "Two invented pipelines, one per autoscaler. Image workers scale on CPU with a Kubernetes HPA while Kafka buffers an upload burst; poster render workers sleep at zero until KEDA sees Kafka lag, wake, drain the burst and return to zero. Teaching timings (1 s syncs and polling, 1-2 s startup, short stabilization and cooldown) are deliberately shorter than the published defaults. Open a worker's Live details for replica history."

simulations.title: HPA: image workers absorb a burst

action.text: Demand is above one worker’s target. New replicas start while Kafka holds the backlog.
Ready workers drain the upload burst. Open Live details to see desired and ready replicas over time.

simulations.title: KEDA: render workers wake from zero

action.text: Eighty render requests arrive while no worker runs. KEDA sees the group's lag and wakes one.
HPA takes over from one replica and scales on lag; the backlog drains, then the workers return to zero.
